bbva.intro: BBVA shows solid progress in structuring its 'Net Zero' roadmap between 2024 and 2025, evidenced by the expansion of scope towards key sectors such as Aluminium and cargo Aviation. However, the bank faces transparency challenges arising from methodological restatements in Oil & Gas and an alarming deviation in meeting short-term targets in its Steel portfolio.

points.title: Critical setback and lack of transparency in Steel
points.body: It is essential to focus on the 12% increase in the Steel sector's physical intensity reported in 2025 (p. 166) versus the previous year (p. 158). This sharp rise is presented without any contextual or macroeconomic explanation in the report, undermining the credibility of the 2030 target for this heavy portfolio.

points.title: Break in the historical series in Oil & Gas due to inclusion of 'midstream'
points.body: The change to the base-year absolute emissions of the Oil & Gas portfolio (an increase of 0.6 MtCO2e) improves completeness but breaks the comparability of the progress reported in 2024, constituting a methodological risk as the ambition of the final reduction percentage was not clearly reformulated.

points.title: Impossibility of traceability in the Shipping portfolio
points.body: The adoption of the Poseidon Principles v4 as the governing framework in the 2025 report versus the previous 2024 model hinders continuous transition-risk tracking for maritime assets, requiring a bridge baseline to be established so that investors can measure shipowners' real improvement.

points.title: Strengthening by bringing forward commitments in Coal
points.body: The decision to bring forward by two years (from 2040 to 2038) the target for eliminating global thermal-coal exposure, as certified in the 2025 report's strategic update, is a highly positive signal for the market.
